name: FuseBase (formerly Nimbus Note)
description: Notes, folders, workspaces, tasks, files, portals, databases, and organization resources exposed by FuseBase's customer-owned MCP connection.
agentUseSummary: Connect a FuseBase MCP URL and token, then let agents discover and use the complete provider-granted tool surface under Safe or Dangerously skip permissions policy.

credentialRequirements.name: FUSEBASE_MCP_URL
credentialRequirements.label: FuseBase MCP URL
credentialRequirements.helpText: Copy the remote MCP URL from the FuseBase organization MCP configuration. Relay accepts only official FuseBase HTTPS hosts.

credentialRequirements.name: FUSEBASE_MCP_TOKEN
credentialRequirements.label: FuseBase MCP token
credentialRequirements.helpText: Copy the revocable token shown when the FuseBase MCP configuration is created.

capabilities.label: Tool discovery
capabilities.description: Discover tools granted by the customer-owned FuseBase MCP configuration.

capabilities.label: Read tools
capabilities.description: Call discovered FuseBase tools classified as read-only.

capabilities.label: Full MCP
capabilities.description: Call every FuseBase MCP tool granted by the customer's configuration.

allowed.label: Discover tools
allowed.description: List bounded metadata for provider-granted tools.

allowed.label: Use a read tool
allowed.description: Call a discovered tool whose name is classified as read-only.

approvalRequired.label: Use any granted tool
approvalRequired.description: Call any provider-granted tool; Safe mode requires approval.

approvalProfiles.label: Safe
approvalProfiles.description: Discovery and read-only tools run directly; every other provider-granted tool requires approval.

approvalProfiles.label: Dangerously skip permissions
approvalProfiles.description: Every selected provider-granted tool runs without Relay per-action approval; ownership, provider authority, secret isolation, output bounds, and audit controls still apply.

runtimeSupport.description: Railway mounts selected FuseBase wrappers and proxies the MCP token server-side.
Railway mounts selected FuseBase wrappers and proxies the MCP token server-side.

providerSetup.nextAction: The customer creates a FuseBase MCP configuration with the intended Read, Edit, Full, or custom area authority and enters its URL and token in Relay Console.

evidence.supports: FuseBase owners and managers can create a remote MCP configuration, choose Full, Read, or custom Off/Read/Edit authority by area, receive an MCP URL and token, and revoke it.
Streamable HTTP uses JSON-RPC POST/GET, application/json and text/event-stream responses, protocol-version headers, and optional session IDs.
Clients initialize, negotiate protocol capabilities, send initialized notification, then use tools/list and tools/call.
FuseBase is the current Nimbus Web product, so this candidate is implemented under its current provider identity.
